Current skill passed all 20 expectations; the iteration-1 snapshot passed 17 of 20, a 15 percentage-point gain.
The discriminating gains are narrow and intentional: task-grounded visual references, one justified signature device, and an auditable Emoji-exception approval state.
The vague-project regression case passed 5/5 in both configurations, so the design-focused revision preserved the original blueprint contract.
Many design assertions remain non-discriminating: the snapshot already avoided generic decorative patterns, wrote actionable states, and handled accessibility well.

The eval-7 snapshot run stopped after PRD, SPEC, DESIGN, and domain specs. Its design assertions remain gradeable, but its incomplete artifact set makes total runtime and completeness comparisons unreliable.
Timing is approximate or includes timeout/recovery work in several runs; compare quality scores rather than treating the time delta as a performance result.

Model token counts were unavailable. The benchmark tokens field contains final-output character counts as a consistent review-cost proxy; current outputs averaged 20,874 characters versus 18,006 for the snapshot.
There is one run per configuration per eval. The displayed standard deviation is across different evals, not repeated-run variance.
